title: Compare Each Employee to Their Department Average Salary
description: Show each employee's name, department, salary, their **department's average salary**, the **difference from average**, and a label: **'Above Average'**, **'Below Average'**, or **'Average'**.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE employees (emp_id INT, name VARCHAR(100), department VARCHAR(50), salary INT); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'Alice','Engineering',95000),(2,'Bob','Engineering',85000),(3,'Carol','Engineering',105000),(4,'Dave','Engineering',75000),(5,'Eve','Marketing',65000),(6,'Frank','Marketing',70000),(7,'Grace','Marketing',80000),(8,'Hank','Sales',55000),(9,'Ivy','Sales',60000),(10,'Jack','Sales',72000);
solution_sql: SELECT name, department, salary, ROUND(AVG(salary) OVER (PARTITION BY department), 2) AS dept_avg, salary - ROUND(AVG(salary) OVER (PARTITION BY department), 2) AS diff_from_avg, CASE WHEN salary > AVG(salary) OVER (PARTITION BY department) THEN 'Above Average' WHEN salary < AVG(salary) OVER (PARTITION BY department) THEN 'Below Average' ELSE 'Average' END AS comparison FROM employees ORDER BY department, salary DESC

test_cases.description: 10 employees with dept_avg, diff, and comparison label. Engineering avg=90000, Marketing avg=71667, Sales avg=62333.

hints: Use AVG(salary) OVER (PARTITION BY department) to compute the department average and attach it to every employee row without collapsing the data.
Subtract the window average from salary to get the diff, then use CASE on the same window expression to classify above/below/average.
explanation: AVG(salary) OVER (PARTITION BY department) computes per-department averages and stamps them on every row. Engineering avg=90000: Alice(95k)=Above, Bob(85k)=Below, Carol(105k)=Above, Dave(75k)=Below. This approach avoids a self-join or correlated subquery. The CASE expression uses the window function result directly for classification.
